key_insight: Agensh shows that multi-agent systems can scale far beyond a single orchestrator by letting workers self-organize and coordinate directly. This enables concurrent execution at very large scale, reaching 1,024 agents.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the scalability bottleneck in existing multi-agent harnesses, where a central orchestrator limits task allocation, coordination, and overall throughput as the number of agents grows.
method: Replaces the central orchestrator with a self-organized harness where concurrent workers participate in a shared multi-agent cooperation loop.
Distributes coordination responsibilities across agents to reduce bottlenecks and improve parallelism.
Designs the system to support very large-scale collaboration, demonstrating operation at 1,024 agents.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical path to building larger, faster, and more resilient agentic systems without depending on a single coordination hub. It may enable lower latency on complex tasks and better scalability for production multi-agent applications.
visual_elements: A hub-and-spoke diagram comparing a central orchestrator vs. self-organized agents
An architecture flow showing the cooperation loop among workers
A scalability chart illustrating performance as agent count increases up to 1,024
Icons representing parallel execution, coordination, and distributed control
paper_title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
paper_authors: Zhihao Zhan, Ting Song, Li Dong, Shaohan Huang, Jianxun Lian
